name: AGRITOX
label: AGRITOX
creator: Agence Nationale de Sécurité Sanitaire de l’Alimentation, de l’Environnement et du Travail; Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique
description: French database of pesticide active substances, created by INRA and now run by ANSES. It holds expert-validated data from regulatory dossiers and the literature: identity, physicochemical properties, acute toxicity, reference values (ADI, ARfD, AOEL), ecotoxicity and classification. The data are released as open files, so regulatory pesticide hazard data can be reused.

name: Australian Industrial Chemicals Introduction Scheme
label: AICIS
creator: AICIS (Australian Government)
description: Online database search portal of Australia's industrial chemicals regulator, which replaced National Industrial Chemicals Notification and Assessment Scheme (NICNAS) in July 2020. It gives access to the Australian Inventory of Industrial Chemicals which is a searchable database of around 40,000 chemicals that are being manufactured or imported (introduced) into Australia for industrial use. It included published human-health and environmental hazard, exposure and risk assessments (including reports inherited from NICNAS) and risk-management recommendations.

name: Nanosafety FAIR maturity indicators (Ammar et al.)
label: Nanosafety FAIR maturity indicators…
aliases: Ammar Ammar nanotox fair maturity indicators; 281 maturity indicators; FAIR maturity models/framework for Toxicology; FAIR assessment of nanosafety data reusability with community standards
creator: Maastricht University
description: These are machine-readable FAIR maturity indicators derived from twelve nanosafety minimum reporting standards. The NSDRA framework uses them to annotate nanosafety datasets and score how reusable the datasets are for specific computational risk assessment use cases.

name: Event Components (structured Key Event annotation)
label: Event Components
creator: Environmental Protection Agency; Directorate-General Joint Research Centre
description: A structured way of describing each AOP Key Event as a biological process, a biological object and an action, each term taken from an existing ontology or controlled vocabulary. Implemented in the AOP-Wiki, it makes Key Events machine-readable so AOPs can be searched, compared and linked computationally.

name: Adverse Outcome Pathways Wiki Identifier
label: AOP-WIKI-ID
description: Each AOP is automatically given a numerical AOP identifier by the AOP-Wiki when it is created (e.g., AOP: ###).

name: AOP-DB (Adverse Outcome Pathway Database)
label: AOP-DB
creator: US EPA
description: The US EPA Adverse Outcome Pathway Database (AOP-DB) links AOP information from the AOP-Wiki to public data on genes, chemicals, diseases, pathways, species orthology and ToxCast assays. It supports computational exploration of the molecular targets and biological context of AOPs; this row covers the first version, described in 2018.

name: AOP-DB RDF
label: AOP-DB RDF
creator: US EPA; Maastricht University (BiGCaT)
description: AOP-DB RDF is a semantic-web (RDF) version of selected AOP-DB tables, mapped to ontologies and aligned with AOP-Wiki RDF, and served through a public SPARQL endpoint. It allows federated queries that link AOP data with genes, diseases, pathways and ToxCast assays.

name: AOP Developers' Handbook
label: AOP Developers' Handbook
creator: OECD (EAGMST, now ESCA advisory group)
description: The OECD AOP Developers' Handbook (formerly Users' Handbook) is the supplement to the OECD Guidance Document for developing and assessing AOPs. It specifies what information each AOP, Key Event and Key Event Relationship page in the AOP-Wiki must contain, and how weight of evidence and applicability are to be recorded, so AOP descriptions are structured and comparable for review.

name: AOP-helpFinder 3.0
label: AOP-helpFinder 3.0
fsrType: FAIR Analysis Service; FAIR Enrichment Service; FAIR Visualization Service
creator: Universite Paris Cite / Inserm
description: AOP-helpFinder 3.0 is the third major version of AOP-helpFinder. AOP-helpFinder is a web tool for identification and extraction of associations between stressors and biological events at various level of the biological organization (molecular initiating event (MIE), key event (KE), and adverse outcome (AO)) so researchers can collect literature evidence to build and weigh adverse outcome. The third version adds network views of the stressor-event and event-event (key event relationship) links found by text mining, and annotates them with data from external sources such as AOP-Wiki, KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome, UniProt and disease-gene databases.

name: AOP-networkFinder
label: AOP-networkFinder
creator: Norwegian Institute of Public Health (FHI); University of Oslo
description: AOP-networkFinder is a web application, also available as open code and a Docker image. It pulls content from AOP-Wiki to build, merge, annotate and visualise networks of adverse outcome pathways, and exports them to Cytoscape for further analysis.

name: AOP Ontology (AOPO)
label: AOP Ontology (AOPO)
creator: US Army ERDC (L. Burgoon)
description: An OWL ontology for adverse outcome pathways that reuses classes from existing biomedical ontologies to describe molecular initiating events, key events and adverse outcomes in a common vocabulary. It enables computational reasoning over AOPs, and its terms are reused, for example, in the AOP-Wiki RDF.

name: AOP-Wiki
label: AOP-Wiki
subdomains: AOP-based mechanistic knowledge; computational and predictive toxicology
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; Reference AOP FIP
creator: OECD (with US EPA and EC JRC)
description: The AOP-Wiki is the OECD collaborative wiki for building, reviewing and publishing adverse outcome pathways. It records molecular initiating events, key events, key event relationships, stressors and the supporting evidence in a structured template. Its downloadable content is the central reference store of AOP knowledge for regulatory and computational toxicology.

name: AOP-Wiki RDF
label: AOP-Wiki RDF
creator: Maastricht University (BiGCaT)
description: A Linked Data version of the AOP-Wiki, converted from the AOP-Wiki XML export into RDF and served through a public SPARQL endpoint. The RDF content for all the AOP-Wiki content were mapped with additional semantic annotations, persistent identifiers, and extended identifiers for genes and chemicals, so AOP knowledge can be queried and combined with other resources. The semantic annotation was done using 8 standard metadata vocabularies and 17 domain-specific ontologies and vocabularies.

name: AOP-XML (AOP-Wiki XML exchange format)
label: AOP-XML (AOP-Wiki XML exchange format)
subdomains: AOP-based mechanistic knowledge; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: AOP-Wiki development team (US EPA; SAAOP)
description: The XML schema and exchange format in which the AOP-Wiki exports its full content (AOPs, Key Events, KERs, stressors, Event Components and evidence fields), published as nightly and quarterly frozen downloads. It is the machine-readable source that downstream resources such as AOP-Wiki RDF and AOP-DB are built from.

name: AOP Xplorer
label: AOP Xplorer
subdomains: AOP-based mechanistic knowledge; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: US Army Engineer Research and Development Center (Lyle Burgoon)
description: AOPXplorer is a Cytoscape app with companion R packages that builds AOP networks from the AOP Ontology and overlays user data, such as gene expression, on them. It was the AOP-KB module for viewing AOPs in a wider network context.

name: The Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority (APVMA) database of completed chemical reviews
label: APVMA-CR
creator: APVMA
description: Listing of chemical reviews by the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority: completed, ongoing and scheduled reconsiderations of registered agricultural and veterinary chemicals. Review reports document human-health, environmental, residue and worker-safety assessments and the resulting regulatory decisions.

name: ArrayExpress
label: ArrayExpress
sources: FAIRsharing Toxicology collection; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: Public EMBL-EBI archive for functional genomics experiments, mainly gene expression data from microarrays and high-throughput sequencing (including single-cell), annotated to MIAME and MINSEQE. Now served through BioStudies but with its own data model and Annotare submission tool, it lets toxicogenomics datasets be deposited, found and reused.

name: ArrayTrack
label: ArrayTrack
span: Data generation; Data integration; Regulatory assessment
creator: US FDA NCTR
description: ArrayTrack is FDA NCTR software that combines a MIAME-supportive microarray database, local copies of public annotation libraries and analysis tools. It was used to store, analyse and interpret toxicogenomics and pharmacogenomics data, including genomic data submitted to FDA.

name: BioAssay Ontology (BAO)
label: BioAssay Ontology (BAO)
creator: University of Miami
description: The BioAssay Ontology (BAO) is an OWL ontology that describes biological screening assays and their results, including assay format, design, detection technology, target and endpoint. It allows bioassay and high-throughput screening data (for example from PubChem) to be annotated consistently, queried and integrated.

name: Biochemical and Chemical Entity Vocabulary
label: Biochemical and Chemical Entity…
creator: PARC (Human Biomonitoring community) / VITO
description: The Biochemical and Chemical Entity Vocabulary describes the bio(chemical) entities measured in the humam body and monitored in the environment related to the research studies within the PARC HBM Community.

name: BioImage Archive
label: BioImage Archive
creator: European Bioinformatics Institute
description: EMBL-EBI's public archive for biological images from any imaging modality and scale, from molecules to whole organisms, for datasets linked to a publication or of value beyond a single experiment; patient-identifiable medical images are excluded. It implements the REMBI metadata guidelines, archives data for related image resources such as EMPIAR and IDR, and is adding OME-Zarr access for interactive viewing and streaming.

name: BioModels
label: BioModels
creator: European Bioinformatics Institute
description: A repository of mathematical models of biological processes taken from the literature, many of them manually curated, annotated and checked for reproducibility, mostly in SBML. Models get stable identifiers and semantic annotations, so they can be found, cited, simulated and reused, including in quantitative systems toxicology and PBK modelling.

name: Bioschemas
label: Bioschemas
description: Bioschemas is an open community initiative, supported by ELIXIR, that helps life-science websites describe their resources with schema.org markup so that search engines and registries can find them. It proposes new life-science types and properties to schema.org and publishes profiles that state which properties to use, graded minimum, recommended or optional, for datasets, tools, samples, chemicals, training materials and other resources.

name: Bioschemas ChemicalSubstance Profile
label: Bioschemas ChemicalSubstance Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: Bioschemas profile that sets out which schema.org properties (identifiers, names, composition, links to ChEBI and other ontology terms) to use when marking up web pages about chemical substances. Substance records on websites and databases then become findable by search engines and harvesters and interoperable as structured metadata.

name: Bioschemas ComputationalTool Profile
label: Bioschemas ComputationalTool Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: Bioschemas profile for describing software tools and services with schema.org markup: name, function, inputs and outputs, version, operating system, licence and citation, using EDAM terms as in bio.tools. It makes research software, including in silico toxicology tools, findable and comparable on the web.

name: Bioschemas ComputationalWorkflow Profile
label: Bioschemas ComputationalWorkflow Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: Bioschemas profile that defines schema.org metadata for computational workflows (creators, workflow language, inputs and outputs as formal parameters, licence, version), so that workflows can be described, found and cited, for example in WorkflowHub and Workflow RO-Crate. It supports FAIR sharing of analysis pipelines, including those used in toxicology.

name: Bioschemas Dataset Profile
label: Bioschemas Dataset Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: The Bioschemas Dataset Profile is a metadata profile (metadata schema) developed by the Bioschemas community to describe life-science datasets using structured metadata based on the Schema.org Dataset type and is graded as minimum, recommended or optional. Consistent markup lets search engines, registries and portals harvest dataset descriptions, so datasets are easier to find across repositories.

name: Bioschemas Deploys
label: Bioschemas Deploys
creator: ELIXIR Bioschemas Community
description: Lists the sites that use Bioschemas markup to - a direct link to the site, an example deployment page, and a link to test the markup syntax using the Schema.org Markup Validation tool is provided.

name: Bioschemas MolecularEntity Profile
label: Bioschemas MolecularEntity Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: A Bioschemas profile for describing molecular or chemical entities such as small molecules, drugs, metabolites on web pages with schema.org properties (e.g., names, identifiers,  InChI, InChIKey, SMILES, molecular formula, biological or chemical roles, links to ChEBI, PubChem, ChemSpider, or other database). Chemical records on different sites can then be harvested and linked through shared structured metadata.

name: Bioschemas Sample Profile
label: Bioschemas Sample Profile
creator: Bioschemas community (ELIXIR)
description: A Bioschemas profile with a minimal set of schema.org properties, plus Bioschemas extensions, to identify, link and describe biological samples on web pages. Biobanks and sample databases can then expose comparable sample metadata that search engines and aggregators can harvest.

name: Bioschemas TrainingMaterial Profile
label: Bioschemas TrainingMaterial Profile
description: A Bioschemas profile, built on the schema.org LearningResource type, that sets out the properties for marking up life-science training materials on web pages: a minimum of name, description, keywords and the profile it conforms to, plus recommended ones such as audience, prerequisites, learning outcomes and licence. Materials marked up this way can be harvested automatically by training registries such as ELIXIR TeSS and by search engines.

name: BioSamples
label: BioSamples
sources: FAIRsharing Toxicology collection; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: European Bioinformatics Institute
description: EMBL-EBI database that stores and curates metadata about biological samples used in assays and gives each one a stable accession. Samples are either 'reference' samples (e.g. from 1000 Genomes, HipSci, FAANG) or experimental samples, and have been used in an assay that has generated publicly available data in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) or ArrayExpress. BioSamples supports links between sample records and any sample-derived datasets, including sequence-based datasets such as those held in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) or ArrayExpress, -omics-based datasets such as those in PRIDE or MetaboLights, and any other assay-based databases. It provides links to assays and specific samples and accepts direct submissions of sample information.

name: BioStudies
label: BioStudies
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: European Bioinformatics Institute
description: An EMBL-EBI archive for whole biological studies. It stores study-level metadata, links to data held in other archives, and data files that have no dedicated repository. It hosts project collections, including those of toxicology projects, and now holds the ArrayExpress functional genomics data.

name: Biocides in the environment
label: Biocides in the environment
creator: German Environment Agency
description: Database of the German Environment Agency on the ChemInfo platform. The site provides environmental monitoring data for biocidal substances from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, including measurements in water, wastewater, soil, sediment, sewage sludge, and biota, together with approval status, physicochemical properties and CLP classification. Environmental occurrence data for biocides can be searched and exported.

name: The Blood Exposome Database
label: The Blood Exposome Database
creator: University of California, Davis
description: The Blood Exposome Database catalogues the chemicals (endogenous and exogenous) that are expected and detected in human blood specimens. The database was created using a text mining approach using the NCBI PubChem , NCBI PubMed and NCBI PMC databases. Additionally, data from biomonitoring surveys and metabolomics datasets (publicly available) for human blood specimens are also covered in the database. It supports exposome research and the annotation of untargeted metabolomics and exposomics data.

name: CAS Registry Number
label: CAS Registry Number
creator: CAS (Chemical Abstracts Service), American Chemical Society
description: Numeric identifier, up to ten digits in three hyphenated parts ending in a check digit, that CAS assigns to each distinct substance in its CAS REGISTRY. It is the most widely used substance identifier in chemical inventories, regulations and safety data, and links names and data across sources.

name: Chemical Effects in Biological Systems
label: CEBS
creator: NIEHS and the US National Toxicology Program
description: Public NIEHS repository of toxicology study data: the individual-animal and summary data of the US National Toxicology Program studies, and data deposited by academic, industrial and government laboratories, held with their study design so that studies can be compared and combined. It holds the NTP data collections (now DTT Data Collections) and the complete DrugMatrix database.

name: Cellosaurus
label: Cellosaurus
creator: SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics (CALIPHO group)
description: Cellosaurus is a curated knowledge resource on cell lines used in research. Each cell line has a stable accession, also used as its RRID, with names, synonyms, species, origin, STR profile, known contamination or misidentification and cross-references, so cell lines can be identified, cited and linked across databases.

name: Common European Research Information Format
label: CERIF
fsrType: Metadata schema; Provenance model; Semantic model; Structured vocabulary
creator: European Commission; euroCRIS
description: CERIF is a data model for research information that represents research entities such as projects, their activities and outputs, and the typed relationships between them. Recommended by the European Commission to EU Member States, it supports exchange between current research information systems.

name: Canada’s Existing Substances Assessment Repository
label: CESAR
creator: Environment and Climate Change Canada; Health Canada
description: Canadian repository of risk and other regulatory assessment reports on existing substances under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, from the Priority Substances List and the Chemicals Management Plan. Each report covers substance identity, exposure, effects and risk characterisation. Reports are reached through eChemPortal and Health Canada's chemical substances portal.

name: ChEBI (Chemical Entities of Biological Interest)
label: ChEBI
subdomains: conventional toxicology; nanotoxicology; computational and predictive toxicology
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: ChEBI (Chemical Entities of Biological Interest) is a freely available dictionary and ontology of small molecular entities, classified by chemical structure and by biological or application role. Its stable identifiers, names, structures and cross-references are widely used to annotate chemicals in databases and ontologies.

name: ChEMBL
label: ChEMBL
sources: FAIRsharing Toxicology collection; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: Open, manually curated database of bioactive, drug-like molecules that links chemical structures to bioactivity measurements, assays and targets, mostly extracted from the medicinal chemistry literature. Its standardised, downloadable data support in silico modelling, including of off-target and toxicity-related activities.

name: ChemInfo
label: ChemInfo
creator: German federal and Länder authorities (ChemInfo cooperation, UBA)
description: Chemical information system managed jointly by the German federal and state authorities as the successor of the GSBL substance data pool. For each substance it compiles identity, physicochemical, toxicological and ecotoxicological data, environmental occurrence, hazard and emergency-response information and the relevant legal provisions. A subset of information can be searched without registration by the user; the full data set is open to authorities and emergency services.

name: ChemSpider
label: ChemSpider
creator: ChemZoo; Royal Society of Chemistry
description: Free chemical structure database, now run by the Royal Society of Chemistry. It merges compounds from hundreds of data sources into structure-based records with names, identifiers, properties and links back to the sources. It helps resolve chemical identity and locate data on a substance.

name: Cell Ontology (CL)
label: Cell Ontology (CL)
creator: Cell Ontology community (OBO Foundry); originally Univ. of Edinburgh, Carnegie Institution, Univ. of Cambridge
description: The Cell Ontology (CL) is an OBO Foundry ontology of cell types across organisms, with definitions and links to anatomy and other ontologies. It gives standard terms for annotating the cell types used in experiments and recorded in datasets.

name: Cell Line Ontology
label: Cell Line Ontology
creator: University of Michigan (CLO Consortium)
description: The Cell Line Ontology (CLO) is an OWL ontology of cell lines, each linked to its species, anatomical origin, cell type, disease and source repository. Built on OBO Foundry ontologies, it gives cell lines stable identifiers and logical definitions for annotating, querying and integrating cell-based data.

name: COMBINE (Computational Modeling in Biology Network) FAIRsharing collection
label: COMBINE (Computational Modeling…
creator: COMBINE (with FAIRsharing)
description: A FAIRsharing collection, maintained  with the COMBINE network, that groups the community standards for computational modelling in biology (e.g. SBML, CellML, SED-ML, SBGN and the COMBINE archive format) with related resources. It gives modellers one curated entry point to interoperable formats for exchanging and annotating computational models in biology.

name: EPA CompTox Chemicals Dashboard
label: EPA CompTox Chemicals Dashboard
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: US EPA web application built on the curated DSSTox substance and structure database for about a million chemicals.  The available data includes, but is not limited to, chemical properties, environmental fate and transport, hazard (e.g., point of departure, legacy toxicity values, screening levels, exposure limits), in vitro to in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE), exposure, use categories, toxic release inventory, monitoring data), bioactivity (e.g., high-throughput data from ToxCast and Tox21 efforts).Batch search, identifier mapping and downloads make these data reusable for computational toxicology and risk assessment.

name: FAIR Cookbook
label: FAIR Cookbook
creator: FAIRplus / ELIXIR
description: An open online collection of practical recipes that show step by step how to make life-science data findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable. Topics include identifiers, metadata, vocabularies, licensing and FAIRness assessment. Domain experts write and review the recipes, and communities, including toxicology, can add their own.

name: Cosmetic ingredient database
label: Cosmetic ingredient database
creator: European Commission (DG GROW)
description: European Commission information database on cosmetic substances and ingredients. It gives INCI names, CAS/EC numbers, functions and regulatory status under EU cosmetics law (annex entries and restrictions back to 1976), with links to scientific committee opinions. It has no legal value, but it makes the regulatory status of an ingredient easy to find.

name: CRED (Criteria for Reporting and Evaluating ecotoxicity Data)
label: CRED
creator: Swiss Ecotox Centre; RIVM; Stockholm University
description: A method for evaluating the reliability (20 criteria) and relevance (13 criteria) of aquatic ecotoxicity studies, with reporting recommendations and an Excel evaluation tool. It makes study evaluations transparent and consistent, so peer-reviewed ecotoxicity data can be reused in regulatory hazard and risk assessment.

name: Comparative Toxicogenomics Database
label: CTD
creator: MDI Biological Laboratory; NC State University
description: Public knowledgebase in which curators extract chemical-gene, chemical-disease, gene-disease and chemical exposure relationships from the literature. These are integrated with external data such as GO and pathways to infer chemical-gene-disease networks. It helps generate hypotheses on how environmental chemicals affect human health.

name: CURE principles for computational models
label: CURE
aliases: CURE; CURE framework; From FAIR to CURE
description: Guidelines proposing that computational models of biological systems, especially mechanistic models in medicine, physiology and systems biology, be Credible, Understandable, Reproducible and Extensible (CURE), as a complement to the FAIR principles.

name: Danish (Q)SAR Database
label: Danish (Q)SAR Database
creator: DTU National Food Institute (first version from the Danish EPA QSAR group, with ECB support)
description: Searchable database of (Q)SAR predictions for a large inventory of chemicals. It covers physicochemical, environmental fate, ecotoxicity, ADME and human health endpoints, uses commercial, free and DTU-built models, and documents each model in QMRF format. It is used to screen and prioritise chemicals and to support classification in chemical regulation.

name: Data Stewardship Wizard (DS-Wizard)
label: Data Stewardship Wizard (DS-Wizard)
description: The Data Stewardship Wizard is an open-source web platform for writing data management plans together, developed within ELIXIR and begun at the Czech Technical University in Prague. Data stewards encode guidance as knowledge models that drive adaptive questionnaires, and the answers are exported through document templates as readable or machine-actionable plans. Organisations can run their own instances, and the FIP Wizard is built on it.

name: DataCite Metadata Scheme
label: DataCite Metadata Scheme
fsrType: Metadata schema; Provenance model; Semantic model
creator: DataCite
description: The DataCite Metadata Schema is a set of core properties, with documentation and an XML schema, for describing research outputs registered with DataCite DOIs. Its mandatory and recommended properties support accurate identification, citation and retrieval of datasets and other resources. The ontology is available in https://www.sparontologies.net/ontologies

name: EURL ECVAM Database Service on Alternative Methods to Animal Experimentation
label: DB-ALM
creator: European Commission Joint Research Centre (EURL ECVAM)
description: Database service of EURL ECVAM at the JRC that gathered expert-reviewed summaries and step-by-step protocols of non-animal test methods, with test results and validation studies. Its numbered records could be searched by topic, endpoint and test system; the content is now kept as a downloadable static dataset with a DOI.

name: dbZach
label: dbZach
creator: Zacharewski laboratory, Michigan State University
description: Relational database of the Zacharewski laboratory at Michigan State University for toxicology and toxicogenomics data, with tools to enter, retrieve and mine them: genes, clones, sample annotation and protocols, microarray, Affymetrix, real-time PCR and toxicology data, and gene regulation, pathway and orthology information, compliant with MIAME. It is no longer accessible.

name: DC Data Explorer
label: DC Data Explorer
subdomains: conventional toxicology; toxicogenomics; AOP-based mechanistic knowledge; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: Edelweiss Connect (Switzerland)
description: DC Data Explorer is a Douglas Connect web interface with REST APIs. It gives harmonised programmatic access to the US EPA ToxCast/Tox21 and ToxRefDB data and to the Open TG-GATEs toxicogenomics data, so users can search across these sources and pull the data into workflow tools.

name: Diamonds (TNO)
label: Diamonds (TNO)
creator: Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research
description: DIAMONDS brings together Data, Knowledge and Algorithms from Clinical studies to Omics data to Personalized Health data. Traceable from original Raw measurements to Cleaned, Processed data ready to use. Knowledge ranges from Biological Knowledge from Curated databases and Textmining to manually Curated Triples from TNO experts. All are captured and connected to Source information through Standardized Pipelines and Workflows Protocols. Diverse tools and algorithms such as Statistical tools, Text mining methods, Scripts, Decision Trees, Bayesian/Dynamic Networks and Network Visualization. Only few resources are publically available.

name: diXa data infrastructure for chemical safety assessment
label: diXa
creatorType: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
creator: diXa consortium (Maastricht University, EMBL-EBI)
description: A data infrastructure from the EU FP7 diXa project that connected a central toxicogenomics data warehouse at EMBL-EBI to a portal linking chemical, molecular and phenotype information. It offered online templates and guidelines for depositing data, plus tools for analysing them; the service is no longer online.

name: Digital Object Identifier
label: Digital Object Identifier
sources: Reference AOP FIP; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: International DOI Foundation
description: The Digital Object Identifier system, standardised as ISO 26324 and built on the Handle System, assigns persistent identifiers to digital objects such as articles and datasets. The doi.org resolver turns each DOI into the object's current location and metadata, so references stay stable when content moves.

name: DrugMatrix
label: DrugMatrix
creator: Iconix Pharmaceuticals; US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS) from late 2010
description: Toxicogenomics reference database of short-term rat studies of about 600 drugs and other chemicals: gene expression in up to seven tissues and in cultured rat hepatocytes, paired with histopathology, clinical chemistry, haematology and in vitro pharmacology assays. Built by Iconix Pharmaceuticals, it was taken over by the US National Toxicology Program in late 2010 and made free; the complete database is now in CEBS and the gene expression data in GEO.

name: Dryad Digital Repository
label: Dryad Digital Repository
creator: National Evolutionary Synthesis Center (NESCent); Dryad
description: Dryad is a non-profit, general-purpose repository that curates and publishes the data underlying research from all disciplines. Each dataset receives a DataCite DOI and is released under CC0, which makes the data findable, citable and reusable, and connects it to the article it supports.

name: Dietary Supplement Label Database
label: DSLD
creator: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements (ODS) and National Library of Medicine (NLM)
description: The Dietary Supplement Label Database (DSLD) is a publicly accessible database maintained by the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH) Office of Dietary Supplements. It contains current and historical label information from dietary supplement products marketed in the United States (ingredients and amounts, label claims, warnings and label images) for current and historical products, searchable online and downloadable through an API. It supports research on supplement composition and exposure, including screening for potentially harmful ingredients.

name: DSSTox
label: DSSTox
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: US EPA's curated database of chemical substances, in which each substance's names and CAS Registry Numbers are linked to one accurate chemical structure and a permanent DSSTox substance identifier (DTXSID). It covers more than a million substances on lists of interest to EPA and other agencies and is the chemistry foundation of the CompTox Chemicals Dashboard, so that toxicity, bioactivity and property data can be associated with the right chemical and used in structure-based models.

name: EC Inventory
label: EC Inventory
creator: European Commission (JRC); ECHA
description: Combined EU list of EINECS (substances on the market between 1971 and 1981), ELINCS (notified new substances) and the No-Longer-Polymers list, now maintained by ECHA. It assigns the EC numbers that identify substances in EU chemicals legislation and provides reference names for regulatory submissions.

name: ECHA Biocidal Products Regulation
label: ECHA-BPR
creator: ECHA
description: ECHA database of biocidal active substances, organised by active substance and product type. For each it shows approval status under the Biocidal Products Regulation, whether it is a candidate for substitution, and links to assessment reports and authorised products. It makes the outcome of EU biocide evaluations publicly accessible.

name: ECHA CHEM
label: ECHA CHEM
creator: ECHA
description: ECHA's public chemicals database. Its first release published the non-confidential content of all REACH registration dossiers: substance identity, physicochemical, toxicological and ecotoxicological data and safe-use information. It is gradually absorbing ECHA's other public chemical data, such as the C&L Inventory.

name: OECD eChemPortal
label: OECD eChemPortal
creator: Organisation de Coopération et de Développement Economiques
description: OECD eChemPortal is a global chemical information portal developed by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) that provides a single point of access to chemical property, hazard, exposure, and risk assessment information  and GHS classifications, with direct links to the source records from numerous national and international databases.

name: ECOTOXicology Knowledgebase
label: ECOTOXicology Knowledgebase
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: US EPA knowledgebase of curated single-chemical toxicity test results for aquatic organisms, terrestrial plants and wildlife, taken from the literature and coded with controlled vocabularies. Its searchable, downloadable records, linked to other chemical resources, support ecological risk assessment, water-quality criteria, and model development.

name: Ecotoxicology thesaurus
label: Ecotoxicology thesaurus
creator: Institut de l'Information Scientifique et Technique
description: A bilingual French-English SKOS thesaurus of about 4,700 ecotoxicology concepts, published by INIST-CNRS on the Loterre platform. It covers pollutants and their effects on ecosystems and human health. It also contains terms from geography, animal and plant taxonomy and chemical compounds. It uses polyhierarchy. Concepts are grouped into semantic categories. It provides controlled, linkable terms with synonyms for indexing and searching ecotoxicology literature and data.

name: EDAM Bioimaging Ontology
label: EDAM Bioimaging Ontology
creator: EDAM Community (open source)
description: An ontology of imaging and related techniques and technologies, image processing and analysis, image data and formats, within bio- and other sciences. EDAM Bioimaging is an extension to the EDAM ontology (edamontology.org), dedicated to imaging and (bio)image informatics.

name: eData
label: eData
creator: NIVA
description: eData is a data entry and formatting Shiny application (app) in the Source to Outcome Pathway/Risk Assessment Database family, designed to make extracting data on chemical concentrations in the environment from papers and reports easier.

name: EdelweissData
label: EdelweissData
creator: Edelweiss Connect
description: A data management and publishing platform from Edelweiss Connect that ingests, annotates, harmonises and versions tabular datasets and serves them through a web interface and a query API. Its public instance hosts toxicology-related datasets, including in vitro and QSAR data.

name: Effectopedia
label: Effectopedia
subdomains: AOP-based mechanistic knowledge; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: OECD (developed by Hristo Aladjov)
description: Effectopedia was the AOP-KB module for building structured and quantitative AOPs collaboratively. AOPs were drawn as diagrams whose elements carried test methods, experimental dose-response data and computational models. It was open-source desktop software (GPLv3) connected to a central OECD database, and it supported the AOP-XML format and OECD Harmonised Template 201.

name: EFSA statement on the interpretation of FAIR principles for mechanistic effect models in the regulatory environmental risk assessment of pesticides
label: EFSA FAIR statement
aliases: EFSA FAIR statement; EFSA FAIR statement for mechanistic effect models
span: Data generation; Data integration; Regulatory assessment
description: This EFSA statement interprets the FAIR principles for mechanistic effect models used in the environmental risk assessment of pesticides. It covers the underlying data, the model code and the model assessment, lists supporting resources, and gives recommendations for putting the principles into practice.

name: The European Genome-phenome Archive
label: EGA
description:
The European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) is a global network for permanent archiving and sharing of personally identifiable genetic, phenotypic, and clinical data generated for the purposes of biomedical research projects or in the context of research-focused healthcare systems.

The EGA is jointly managed by the European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI) in Cambridge (UK) and the Centre for Genomic Regulation (CRG) in Barcelona

name: ELIXIR Deposition Databases
label: ELIXIR Deposition Databases
creator: ELIXIR
description: ELIXIR's list of recommended repositories for depositing experimental life-science data, chosen against technical-quality and governance criteria in line with the FAIR principles. It points researchers, funders and publishers to suitable archives (e.g. ENA, ArrayExpress/BioStudies, PRIDE, MetaboLights, BioModels) for publishing open data.

name: ELIXIR Learning Paths Handbook
label: ELIXIR Learning Paths Handbook
description: The ELIXIR Learning Paths Handbook, by the ELIXIR Training Platform, sets out a six-step protocol for designing learning paths: ordered sequences of courses and training materials that take learners step by step towards defined skills on a subject. It is still under development, and ELIXIR learning paths built with the protocol are curated and published in TeSS.

name: Electron Microscopy Public Image Archive
label: EMPIAR
fsrType: Domain-specific registry; Identifier service; Metadata-data linking schema
creator: EMBL's European Bioinformatics Institute
description: The Electron Microscopy Public Image Archive is a public resource for raw images underpinning 3D cryo-EM maps and tomograms (themselves archived in EMDB). EMPIAR also accommodates 3D datasets obtained with volume EM techniques and soft and hard X-ray tomography. All data archived in EMPIAR can be re-used freely without any conditions or restrictions ("CC0" license model).

name: eNanoMapper database
label: eNanoMapper database
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; FAIRsharing Toxicology collection
creator: eNanoMapper consortium (Ideaconsult)
description: A public database, built by Ideaconsult on its AMBIT software within the eNanoMapper project, that holds nanomaterial characterisation data together with biological and toxicological study results. Data can be uploaded via configurable spreadsheet templates, searched, and downloaded in several standard formats through a web interface and REST API.

name: eNanoMapper ontology
label: eNanoMapper ontology
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; FAIRsharing Toxicology collection
creator: eNanoMapper consortium (EMBL-EBI, Maastricht University)
description: An OWL ontology for nanomaterial safety that assembles slimmed modules from existing ontologies such as ChEBI, NPO, BAO and OBI and adds nano-specific classes. It supplies the shared vocabulary for annotating nanomaterials, their characterisation and toxicity assays in eNanoMapper-based databases.

name: Ensembl
label: Ensembl
sources: FAIRsharing Toxicology collection; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: European Bioinformatics Institute; Wellcome Sanger Institute
description: Ensembl is a core part of the freely available data services hosted by EMBL's European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI). Ensembl generates and imports genome annotation such as genes, variation, regulation and comparative genomics for vertebrates, non-vertebrates and key model organisms, and makes this information available through the web, APIs and bulk downloads. The website provides visualisations and functionality that enable the manipulation and analysis of this data. Toxicology uses it to map, identify and annotate genes in omics data.

name: Environment Ontology
label: Environment Ontology
creator: EnvO Consortium (from the Genomic Standards Consortium)
description: ENVO is a community ontology in OBO foundry of environmental entities of all kinds, from microscopic to intergalactic scales. ENVO currently deals with 'environmental systems' (i.e. environments) particularly 'biomes' and environments determined by a material entity that assumes the role of an 'environmental feature' (e.g. a digestive tract environment). It also handles 'environmental materials' like soil, water.

name: EPA Aquatic Life Benchmarks
label: EPA Aquatic Life Benchmarks
creator: US EPA (Office of Pesticide Programs)
description: Table from EPA's Office of Pesticide Programs (OPP) giving freshwater toxicity benchmarks for registered pesticides and their degradation products: acute and chronic values for fish, invertebrates and plants. For each of the chemicals listed, the table provides a link to the source documents from which each of the benchmarks is extracted.  EPA uses Harmonized Test Guidelines and the Evaluation Guidelines for Ecological Toxicity Data in the Open Literature to evaluate the quality and utility of the studies. The toxicity data used to develop Aquatic Life Benchmarks are extracted from the most recent publicly available OPP risk assessment for the individual pesticide and are typically based on the most sensitive value for each taxon. Aquatic Life Benchmarks are estimates of the concentrations below which pesticides are not expected to represent a risk of concern for aquatic life. The Office of Water criteria shows where risks exist. It is used by State, tribal, and local governments  to interpret pesticide levels measured in water and to decide which sites to follow up.

name: Chemical Data Reporting (CDR) public data
label: Chemical Data Reporting (CDR) public…
creator: US EPA
description: Manufacturing, processing and use data that companies report to the US EPA under the Toxic Substances Control Act.

name: Consolidated Human Activity Database (CHAD)
label: Consolidated Human Activity Database…
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: Human activity diaries compiled from many studies, used to model how people come into contact with chemicals.

name: EPA ChemView
label: EPA ChemView
creator: US EPA (Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention)
description: US EPA web database that brings together, per chemical, health and safety data submitted under the Toxic Substances Control Act and EPA's own assessments and regulatory actions (such as significant new use rules), with summary templates, links to source documents and export. It makes non-confidential TSCA chemical information findable and reusable.

name: Chemical and Products Database (CPDat)
label: Chemical and Products Database (CPDat)
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: Chemical use and product composition data for exposure assessment, released in versions with DOIs on the EPA CompTox figshare portal.

name: EPA Integrated Risk Information System
label: EPA IRIS
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: US EPA programme and database of human health hazard assessments of chemicals,  which includes toxicity values such as oral reference doses and inhalation reference concentrations from chronic exposures and cancer hazard assessments,  inhalation unit risks. It gives agencies and others a consistent, citable source of human-health toxicity values for risk assessment erived from scientific evaluations of the available toxicological, epidemiological, and mechanistic evidence for chemicals.

name: NaKnowBase
label: NaKnowBase
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: Relational database of physicochemical and toxicity data on engineered nanomaterials from US EPA research.

name: National Recommended Aquatic Life Criteria
label: National Recommended Aquatic Life…
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: The US EPA's national recommended water quality criteria for the protection of aquatic life.

name: SEMS Superfund Site Contaminant Records
label: SEMS Superfund Site Contaminant Records
creator: US EPA
description: Contaminant records of US Superfund sites in the Superfund Enterprise Management System.

name: EPA Substance Registry Services
label: EPA Substance Registry Services
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: EPA's central registry of the chemicals, biological organisms and other substances that EPA tracks or regulates. Each substance gets an EPA identifier with its names, synonyms and CAS number, and links to the EPA programmes, lists and regulations that cover it, so substances are identified the same way across EPA data systems.

name: Toxicity Reference Database (ToxRefDB)
label: Toxicity Reference Database (ToxRefDB)
subdomains: conventional toxicology; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: Results of in vivo animal toxicity studies for chemicals, released in versions with DOIs on the EPA CompTox figshare portal.

name: Toxicity Values Database (ToxValDB)
label: Toxicity Values Database (ToxValDB)
subdomains: conventional toxicology; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: Toxicity values such as points of departure and reference doses compiled from many sources, released in versions with DOIs on the EPA CompTox figshare portal.

name: TRI Basic Plus data files
label: TRI Basic Plus data files
creator: US EPA
description: Facility-level releases and waste management of toxic chemicals that US facilities report each year to the Toxics Release Inventory, from 1987.

name: UCMR 5 Drinking-Water Contaminant Occurrence Data
label: UCMR 5 Drinking-Water Contaminant…
creator: Environmental Protection Agency
description: Occurrence data for unregulated contaminants in US drinking water from the fifth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule.

name: Chromium Epigenomics Toxicology
label: EpiCrDB
creator: University of Cincinnati (Puga laboratory)
description: University of Cincinnati web portal giving FAIR access to epigenomics datasets (ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, MNase-seq, FAIRE) on how hexavalent chromium disturbs chromatin organisation. It adds curated chemical, cell, antibody and treatment metadata, with links to GEO, BioProject and PubMed.

name: ERM Identifier Database
label: ERM Identifier Database
creator: NanoCommons
description: The European Registry of Materials is a simple registry with the sole purpose to mint material identifiers to be used by research projects throughout the life cycle of their project. The identifier is nothing more than that identifier, and not by default linked to any information.

name: European Union Observatory for Nanomaterials
label: EUON
creator: ECHA (for the European Commission)
description: Observatory website hosted by ECHA that gives neutral public information, in all EU languages, on nanomaterials on the EU market: their uses, safety, regulation and research. It links to searchable nanomaterial data such as registered nanoforms and related databases and studies.

name: European Registry of Materials identifiers (ERM ID)
label: European Registry of Materials…
description: A registry that mints global, unique identifiers (ERM followed by eight digits) for nanomaterials and other materials studied in research projects, including materials whose composition is not disclosed and specific batches or variants. Projects reserve an identifier when they plan to study a material, so that internal documents, datasets and publications refer to the same material and can later be linked to its public data; the identifiers resolve through identifiers.org.

name: EU-ToxRisk Knowledge Portal (knowledge infrastructure)
label: EU-ToxRisk Knowledge Portal
aliases: EU-ToxRisk Knowledge Portal; EU-ToxRisk KI; modular knowledge infrastructure
creator: EU-ToxRisk consortium (Edelweiss Connect)
description: The data and knowledge management infrastructure of the EU-ToxRisk project. It combines a common data and metadata format, a methods database documenting test protocols, data archiving, an API for access to individual data points, analysis notebooks and a knowledge portal. It was built to make in vitro new approach method data from many laboratories documented, shareable and reusable for risk assessment.

name: Exposure Ontology
label: Exposure Ontology
creator: North Carolina State University; Environmental Protection Agency
description: An exposure-science ontology built on four core concepts: exposure stressor, exposure receptor, exposure event and exposure outcome. It was developed with the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database and gives shared terms for capturing exposure data and linking them to toxicology, epidemiology and health data.

name: Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO)
label: Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO)
description: The Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) is an application ontology from EMBL-EBI for the experimental variables recorded in EBI databases, such as diseases, phenotypes, anatomy, cell types and cell lines, chemical compounds and assays. It brings together classes from reference ontologies such as Uberon, ChEBI, the Cell Ontology and MONDO and links them, so that resources such as Expression Atlas, BioSamples, the GWAS Catalog and Open Targets can annotate samples and studies consistently and integrate their data.

name: Exposome Explorer
label: Exposome Explorer
creator: IARC (WHO)
description: Manually curated IARC database of biomarkers of exposure to dietary and environmental risk factors. It records measured concentrations in human biospecimens, the study populations and analytical methods, correlations with external exposure measures, and reproducibility over time. Researchers use it to choose and compare exposure biomarkers for exposome and epidemiological studies.

name: Reference AOP FAIR Implementation Profile
label: Reference AOP FIP
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; Reference AOP FIP
creator: FAIR-AOPs community (GO FAIR Foundation, EC JRC, US EPA)
description: This is the reference FAIR Implementation Profile for adverse outcome pathways. It records which FAIR-enabling resources (identifiers, vocabularies, formats, repositories, licences) the FAIR-AOPs community recommends for each FAIR principle, published as machine-readable nanopublications through the FIP Wizard.

name: FAIR AOP Cluster
label: FAIR AOP Cluster
description: Community that implements the FAIR principles for adverse outcome pathways. It was initiated within the CIAO project and involves the GO FAIR Foundation, the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission, the US Environmental Protection Agency, research and non-profit institutes, and companies.

name: FAIR Connect
label: FAIR Connect
creator: GO FAIR Foundation and IOS Press (now Sage), with CODATA, DTL and Health-RI
description: An open-access platform for FAIR data stewardship where FAIR-supporting resources, FAIR Implementation Profiles and community good practices are published, searched and discussed. It links the human-readable descriptions in the FAIR Connect journal to their machine-readable nanopublications and offers a search engine and dashboard over them.

name: FAIR Lite principles for computational toxicology models
label: FAIR Lite
creator: Cronin et al. 2025
description: The FAIR Lite principles, proposed to ensure the utility of computational toxicology models by making them findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable.

name: FAIR recommendations for in silico predictive toxicology models (Cronin et al., 18 recommendations)
label: FAIR recommendations for in silico…
aliases: Making in silico predictive models for toxicology FAIR; FAIR models (18 recs.)
creator: Cronin et al. 2023
description: Recommendations for making in silico predictive models for toxicology findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable (FAIR), so that models and their predictions can be found, assessed and reused.

name: FAIR Guiding Principles
label: FAIR Guiding Principles
aliases: FAIR principles; FAIR guiding principles; Wilkinson et al. 2016; R1.2; R1.3
creator: FORCE11 (Wilkinson et al. 2016)

name: FAIRsharing
label: FAIRsharing
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: University of Oxford (FAIRsharing team)
description: A curated registry covering all disciplines that lists data and metadata standards, databases and repositories, data policies and collections. The records link to each other and each carries a DOI. It helps researchers, publishers and funders find, choose and cite suitable standards and repositories, and it gives FAIR assessment tools machine-readable descriptions of these resources.

name: FIP Wizard
label: FIP Wizard
creator: GO FAIR Foundation / Data Stewardship Wizard team (CTU Prague) / KnowledgePixels (Tobias Kuhn)
description: A web application built on the Data Stewardship Wizard that guides a community through the FIP questionnaire to declare its FAIR implementation choices for each principle. It publishes the resulting FAIR Implementation Profiles, and any newly declared FAIR-enabling resources, as machine-actionable nanopublications.

name: FIP Matrix tool
label: FIP Matrix tool
aliases: FIP convergence matrix; FAIR Convergence Matrix
fsrType: FAIR Analysis Service; FAIR Visualization Service
creator: Maciej Gromelski
description:
The FAIR (Convergence) Matrix is a tool for comparing multiple FAIR Implementation Profiles (FIPs) side by side across research communities.
While an individual FIP captures the implementation choices of a single community, the matrix aggregates those choices to drive cross-domain harmonization and reuse of proven FAIR Supporting Resources.

name: FAIR Implementation Profile (FIP)
label: FIP
creator: GO FAIR Foundation
description: A FAIR Implementation Profile lists, principle by principle, the FAIR-enabling resources (standards, vocabularies, identifier schemes, repositories, licences) that a community of practice has chosen. FIPs are published as machine-actionable nanopublications, so communities can document, compare and reuse each other's choices and move towards interoperable solutions.

name: Food and Feed Information Portal Database
label: Food and Feed Information Portal…
creator: European Commission (DG SANTE)
description: European Commission portal that brings together EU databases on authorised food and feed substances and products. It covers food additives, enzymes, flavourings and smoke flavourings, feed additives, food contact materials, novel foods, GMOs and health claims, with their authorisation status and conditions of use.

name: File Transfer Protocol
label: File Transfer Protocol
creator: ARPANET Network Working Group; IETF
description: The IETF protocol for moving files between a client and a server over a network. With FTP, people and software can list, download and upload files on remote hosts in a standard way, so data files stay accessible through a widely supported open protocol.

name: F-UJI
label: F-UJI
aliases: F-UJI automated FAIR assessment tool; FUIJ
creator: PANGAEA (FAIRsFAIR)
description: An open-source web service and API that automatically assesses how FAIR a published dataset is, starting from its persistent identifier and applying the FAIRsFAIR data object assessment metrics. It reports scores and test results for each FAIR principle, which repositories and data producers can use to improve their metadata.

name: OECD Guidance Document 211 (describing non-guideline in vitro test methods)
label: OECD Guidance Document 211
creator: OECD
description: OECD guidance with a harmonised template for describing non-guideline in vitro test methods, covering the test system, procedure, data interpretation and performance. It makes method metadata complete and consistent, so regulators can judge whether data from such methods can be used in assessments.

name: OECD Guidance on Good Practices and Standardisation of Sample Collection for Omics Analysis (No. 409)
label: OECD Guidance on Good Practices…
aliases: OECD Series on Testing and Assessment No. 409; ENV/CBC/MONO(2025)8
creator: OECD
description: OECD guidance on the steps before omics analysis: how samples are collected, processed and stored, and how sampling protocols and deviations are recorded, so that omics data from toxicology studies are reliable for regulatory use.

name: OECD Guidance Document on the Generation, Reporting and Use of Research Data for Regulatory Assessments
label: OECD research data guidance
aliases: OECD research data guidance; OECD Guidance Document on research data
creator: OECD
description: OECD guidance on how research data, for example, from academic studies that do not follow test guidelines, should be generated, reported and evaluated so they can be used in regulatory chemical assessments. It sets expectations for documentation and data availability that make such data reusable by regulators.

name: Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO)
label: GEO
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: NCBI
description: NCBI's publically available archive for high-throughput functional genomics data, mostly microarray and sequencing-based gene expression studies. It stores raw and processed data with MIAME-oriented descriptions under stable accessions, so toxicogenomics datasets can be retrieved and reanalysed.

name: GESTIS-Stoffdatenbank
label: GESTIS-Stoffdatenbank
creator: Institute for Occupational Safety and Health of the German Social Accident Insurance (IFA)
description: Information on hazardous substances for safety at work: identity, properties, toxicology, classification and occupational limits.

name: NITE Japan-GHS
label: NITE Japan-GHS
creator: National Institute of Technology and Evaluation
description: Consolidated chemical hazard classification database maintained by the National Institute of Technology and Evaluation (NITE) in Japan. It compiles and publishes the latest GHS (Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals) classification results produced by the Japanese government. For each substance it gives only the latest classification, with hazard categories, label elements and the rationale, as web pages and downloadable Excel lists in Japanese and English. It supports GHS labels and safety data sheets and the reuse of authoritative hazard classifications.

name: GIVIMP (OECD Guidance Document on Good In Vitro Method Practices)
label: GIVIMP
creator: OECD
description: OECD guidance document on Good In Vitro Method Practices (GIVIMP), which sets out the scientific, technical and quality practices for developing and implementing in vitro methods for the regulatory safety assessment of chemicals.

name: Good Laboratory Practice (OECD Principles of GLP)
label: GLP
creator: OECD
description: The OECD Principles of Good Laboratory Practice, a quality system for the organisation and conditions under which non-clinical health and environmental safety studies are planned, performed, monitored, recorded, archived and reported.

name: Gene Ontology (GO)
label: Gene Ontology (GO)
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: Gene Ontology Consortium
description: The Gene Ontology (GO) is a standardized, structured vocabulary describing the functions, processes, and locations/cellular components associated with genes and gene products (proteins and RNAs). The GO is designed to be species-agnostic to enable the annotation of gene products across the entire tree of life.

name: Google Dataset Search
label: Google Dataset Search
description: Google Dataset Search is a free search engine for datasets. It indexes the dataset descriptions that publishers put on their web pages, mostly as schema.org markup, across repositories, publishers, government portals and personal sites. Results link back to the hosting pages, so it makes data findable without storing the data itself.

name: Harvard Dataverse Repository
label: Harvard Dataverse Repository
creator: Institute for Quantitative Social Science (IQSS), Harvard University, with Harvard Library and Harvard University Information Technology
description: Harvard Dataverse is a free, general-purpose research data repository open to researchers in any field. It runs on the open-source Dataverse software and gives each deposited dataset a formal data citation, with search across all hosted collections, so data can be found, cited and reused.

name: HGNC gene symbols
label: HGNC gene symbols
creator: HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee
description: The approved symbols, names and stable identifiers that the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee assigns to human genes, is available through genenames.org. They give each gene one unambiguous label across publications and databases, which is needed to link gene-level toxicology knowledge, such as AOP key events, to other resources.

name: Hypertext Transfer Protocol
label: Hypertext Transfer Protocol
creator: CERN; IETF
description: The application-level protocol of the Web, by which a client requests a resource from a server and receives it with its media type. Data and metadata named by http(s) URIs can be retrieved by any web client, which makes HTTP a basic route to accessibility.

name: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure
label: HTTPS
fsrType: Authentication and authorization service; Communication protocol
creator: Netscape Communications; IETF
description: HTTP carried over an encrypted TLS (formerly SSL) connection. It protects data and credentials in transit and lets a client check the server's identity, so resources named by https URIs can be retrieved securely with a standard open protocol.

name: ILO-WHO International Chemical Safety Cards
label: ICSCs
creator: ILO and WHO (IPCS), with the European Commission
description: Collection of standardised, peer-reviewed data sheets on chemicals, written in standard phrases. Each card gives identity, physical and chemical properties, health and environmental hazards, exposure limits, classification and protective measures; more than 1,700 cards exist in many languages. They give workplaces concise hazard information and can be searched in the ILO ICSC database.

name: Identifiers.org
label: Identifiers.org
subdomains: conventional toxicology; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: Identifiers.org is an EMBL-EBI registry and resolver that gives life-science data collections a namespace prefix and resolves compact identifiers (prefix:accession) and identifiers.org URIs to the matching data record. It makes references to data stable, globally unique and resolvable, which supports the annotation of models and datasets.

name: IGS - Public Informationssystem für gefährliche Stoffe
label: IGS
creator: LANUK NRW (formerly LANUV / Landesumweltamt NRW), Germany
description: Public substance information system of the North Rhine-Westphalia environment agency. For each chemical or microbiological substance it compiles regulatory information from German, EU, Swiss, US and other legislation, together with physical-chemical, toxicological and emergency-response data. The public, authorities and emergency services use it to look up the legal status and hazards of substances.

name: InChI (IUPAC International Chemical Identifier)
label: InChIs
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: IUPAC / NIST / InChI Trust
description: The IUPAC International Chemical Identifier (InChI) is an open algorithm and text string that encodes a chemical structure in a canonical, layered form; the hashed InChIKey is a fixed-length version for searching. It gives chemical substances a unique, machine-readable identifier, so chemical records can be linked and deduplicated across databases.

name: International Harmonization of Nomenclature and Diagnostic criteria
label: INHAND
subdomains: conventional toxicology; nanotoxicology; AOP-based mechanistic knowledge
creator: STP, ESTP, BSTP and JSTP (INHAND initiative)
description: An internationally harmonised nomenclature, with diagnostic criteria, for proliferative and non-proliferative lesions in laboratory animals - it is maintained on the goRENI platform. It standardises how histopathology findings in non-clinical safety studies are recorded and supports the controlled terminology used for regulatory data exchange (SEND).

name: Information Platform for Chemical Monitoring
label: IPCHEM
span: Data generation; Data integration; Regulatory assessment
creator: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC)
description: European Commission platform, hosted by the JRC, for finding and accessing chemical monitoring data collections in four modules: environment, human biomonitoring, food and feed, and products and indoor air. Data come from EU bodies, Member States, international organisations and research projects. It harmonises and quality-checks occurrence data and offers one access point for exposure and risk assessment.

name: Internationally Peer Reviewed Chemical Safety Information
label: IPCS INCHEM
creator: WHO IPCS and CCOHS
description: Free portal from WHO's International Programme on Chemical Safety and the Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety. It gives searchable full-text access to internationally peer-reviewed chemical safety documents, including EHC monographs, CICADs, JECFA and JMPR evaluations, IARC summaries, ICSCs and poisons information monographs.

name: isaconfig-diXa (ISA-Tab configuration for toxicogenomics)
label: isaconfig-diXa
creator: EU FP7 diXa consortium
description: ISAcreator configuration of the diXa project: ISA-Tab templates and controlled fields for describing toxicogenomics studies for deposition in the diXa data warehouse, carrying the study-level fields of SimpleTox into ISA-Tab.

name: ISA-JSON
label: ISA-JSON
creator: University of Oxford
description: ISA-JSON is the JSON serialisation of the ISA (Investigation-Study-Assay) metadata model, defined by JSON schemas and implemented in the ISA-API. It records study design, sample provenance, protocols and data files in machine-actionable form, so metadata can be validated, converted and submitted to repositories.

name: ISA framework (Investigation-Study-Assay; ISA-Tab)
label: ISA
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: European Bioinformatics Institute; University of Oxford
description: The ISA framework is a general Investigation-Study-Assay metadata model, with ISA-Tab as its tab-delimited format and a set of supporting tools, for describing multi-omics and other life-science experiments. It records study design, sample characteristics, protocols and data files, so experimental metadata can be reported consistently, validated and reused.

name: ISA-TAB-Nano
label: ISA-TAB-Nano
creator: NCI caBIG Nanotechnology Working Group
description: Extension of the ISA-Tab format for sharing nanomaterial research data in spreadsheets: a material file describes the nanomaterial and its components, and the study and assay files gain columns for material samples and their characterisation. Specified by the Nanotechnology Working Group of NCI caBIG, it was taken up by nanosafety databases such as the eNanoMapper database.

name: IUCLID (International Uniform Chemical Information Database)
label: IUCLID
creator: European Commission JRC (ECB); since 2008 ECHA with OECD
description: IUCLID is free software for recording, storing, maintaining and exchanging data on the intrinsic and hazard properties of chemical substances. It was developed by the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) in cooperation with the OECD and other regulatory authorities. It implements the OECD Harmonised Templates and is the required format for preparing chemical dossiers for submissions under REACH, the Biocidal Products Regulation and other regulatory programmes.

name: IUPAC Glossary of terms used in immunotoxicology (IUPAC Recommendations 2012)
label: IUPAC immunotox glossary
creator: IUPAC
description: An IUPAC Recommendation that gives agreed definitions, with explanatory notes, for terms used in immunotoxicology. It supports consistent terminology when immunotoxicity data are reported and interpreted.

name: IUPAC Glossary of terms used in toxicology, 2nd edition (IUPAC Recommendations 2007)
label: IUPAC toxicology glossary
aliases: IUPAC toxicology glossary; Glossary Of Terms Used In Toxicology
creator: IUPAC
description: The second edition of IUPAC's glossary of toxicology, giving recommended definitions for terms used in toxicology and chemical risk assessment. It serves as a common reference vocabulary for consistent use of toxicological terms in data and publications.

name: Japan Chemicals Collaborative Knowledge database
label: J-CHECK
creator: NITE with MHLW, METI and MOE (Japan)
description: Japanese government's database on substances covered by the Chemical Substances Control Law (CSCL). It gives the official substance lists and classes; test results on biodegradation, bioaccumulation, ecotoxicity and human toxicity from the existing-chemicals survey and the Japan Challenge Program; and risk assessment outcomes, in Japanese and English. It is linked to the OECD eChemPortal.

name: Japan Existing Chemical Database
label: JECDB
creator: NIHS (MHLW), Japan
description: Database, maintained by the National Institute of Health Sciences (NIHS) of Japan, of toxicity test reports on existing chemicals tested in Japan's safety assessment programme and in the OECD HPV programme, covering acute, repeated-dose, reproductive and developmental, genotoxicity and other tests. It gives English summaries, full reports in Japanese and IUCLID export files.

name: JavaScript Object Notation for Linking Data
label: JSON-LD
creator: W3C
description: A W3C syntax for writing linked data as JSON. A context maps plain JSON keys to IRIs, so web APIs and pages can publish machine-readable metadata, such as schema.org markup, that is also RDF and can be merged with other linked data.

name: Best practices for computational model sharing (Kherroubi Garcia et al.)
label: Best practices for computational model…
creator: Kherroubi Garcia et al. 2025
description: Ten simple rules for sharing computational models in a way that is at least good enough for others to reuse them, and for moving towards better model-sharing practices, as no agreed standard for sharing models exists.

name: Klimisch reliability scoring
label: Klimisch reliability scoring
aliases: Klimisch score; Klimisch et al. framework; Klimisch assignability
creator: Klimisch et al. 1997
description: A systematic approach for evaluating the quality of experimental toxicological and ecotoxicological data, which assigns each study a reliability category (the Klimisch score) for use in hazard and risk assessment.

name: MAGE-ML (MicroArray Gene Expression Markup Language)
label: MAGE-ML
aliases: MAGE-ML; MicroArray Gene Expression Markup Language
creator: FGED (MGED) Society; Object Management Group
description: XML format of the MGED Society for exchanging microarray gene expression data and their annotation, generated from the MAGE object model and adopted by the Object Management Group as its Gene Expression specification. It carried MIAME-compliant data between laboratories, tools and public repositories such as ArrayExpress until the simpler MAGE-TAB replaced it.

name: MAGE-TAB (MicroArray Gene Expression Tabular format)
label: MAGE-TAB
aliases: MAGE-TAB; MicroArray Gene Expression Tabular format
creator: FGED (MGED) Society; EMBL-EBI
description: Tab-delimited, spreadsheet-based format of the MGED Society for MIAME-compliant microarray data and metadata, with an investigation description file (IDF) and a sample and data relationship file (SDRF). It replaced MAGE-ML as the submission format of ArrayExpress, and ISA-Tab shares its syntax.

name: Machine-Actionable OECD Omics Reporting Framework
label: Machine-Actionable OECD Omics Reporting…
creator: PARC Toxicology Community
description: A modular LinkML data model that translates the reporting templates of the OECD Omics Reporting Framework (OORF) into a machine-readable schema, with modules for the study summary, the toxicology experiment, data acquisition and processing (microarray, RNA-seq, qRT-PCR, mass spectrometry, NMR) and data analysis. It lets omics study reports for regulatory toxicology be written, validated and exchanged as structured data. It is a community effort of the PARC toxicology community, still in development and not endorsed by the OECD.

name: MARS (Multi-omics Adapter for Repository Submissions)
label: MARS
creator: ELIXIR (BioHackathon Europe; ELIXIR Data Platform)
description: MARS (Multi-omics Adapter for Repository Submissions) is an ELIXIR framework, with a command-line tool and repository adapters, for submitting a multi-omics study described in ISA-JSON to several public repositories (BioSamples, ENA, MetaboLights) in one go. It aims to keep metadata and accession numbers consistent across those repositories.

name: Extracellular Matrix Interaction Database
label: MatrixDB
creator: CNRS; Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1
description: MatrixDB is a curated database of molecular interactions established by extracellular matrix proteins, proteoglycans, glycosaminoglycans and their bioactive fragments. As a member of the IMEx consortium it offers versioned, exportable interaction data and network views for reuse.

name: MDL Molfile Format
label: MDL Molfile Format
creator: MDL Information Systems (now Dassault Systemes BIOVIA)
description: A plain-text chemical file format from the CTfile family first published by MDL. It stores a molecule's atoms, bonds and coordinates as a connection table with optional property blocks (V2000 and V3000). Almost all cheminformatics software reads it, so it is a standard way to exchange structures, for example as input to QSAR and read-across tools.

name: Medical Subject Headings
label: Medical Subject Headings
creator: US National Library of Medicine
description: Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) is the controlled, hierarchically organised vocabulary of the US National Library of Medicine for indexing, cataloguing and searching biomedical literature, including MEDLINE/PubMed. Its descriptors and entry terms let content written with different words be found under one concept.

name: MetaboLights
label: MetaboLights
creator: EMBL-EBI
description: MetaboLights is an open, cross-species and cross-technique repository for metabolomics studies, holding raw experimental data and their metadata together with reference information on metabolite structures, spectra and biological roles. Journals and ELIXIR recommend it for depositing metabolomics data.

name: MIAME (Minimum Information About a Microarray Experiment)
label: MIAME
creator: FGED (MGED) Society
description: MIAME is a reporting guideline that lists the minimum information needed to interpret and reproduce a microarray experiment: raw and processed data, sample annotation, experimental design, array design and protocols. It underlies the transcriptomics submission requirements of repositories such as GEO and ArrayExpress and of many journals.

name: Minimum Information about Animal Toxicology Experiments
label: MIATE
creator: Michigan State University (Zacharewski lab)
description: A community minimum-information checklist (MIATE/invivo) for the metadata of in vivo animal toxicology studies. It comes with recommended ontologies and templates for CEDAR, GEO, ISA and the Single Cell Portal. Labs can record study design and conditions in a standard form, so animal toxicology and toxicogenomics data can be found and reused.

name: Minimal Information about a high throughput SEQuencing Experiment
label: MINSEQE
creator: FGED Society
description: MINSEQE is a minimum information guideline listing what to report about a high-throughput nucleotide sequencing experiment: samples and variables, raw reads, processed data, sample-data relationships and protocols. Modelled on MIAME, it supports unambiguous interpretation, reproduction and integration of sequencing data.

name: MIRIAM (Minimum Information Requested in the Annotation of biochemical Models)
label: MIRIAM
creator: BioModels.net / COMBINE
description: MIRIAM is a set of minimum-information guidelines for encoding and annotating quantitative biochemical models. It requires models to be reproducible, attributed and annotated with references to external database resources, which encourages reusable, well-documented computational models (for example in BioModels).

name: Minimum Information Reporting in Bio–Nano Experimental Literature
label: Minimum Information Reporting…
description: MIRIBEL is minimum information standard for experimental literature investigating bio–nano interactions. This standard consists of specific components to be reported, divided into three categories: material characterisation, biological characterisation, and details of experimental protocols.

name: Minimum Information Table for the Safety of Engineered Nanomaterials
label: MIT Nanosafety
creator: Leibniz institutes (INM, IUF, IfADo, IWT, FIZ Karlsruhe)
description: A modular minimum information table that sets out what to report with experimental results on the biological effects of engineered nanomaterials. Its six modules are: general information, material information, biological model information, exposure information, endpoint readout information, and analysis and statistics. It supports structured, harmonised documentation of nanosafety studies so the data can be reused.

name: Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB)
label: MSigDB
creator: UC San Diego and Broad Institute
