description: Resource of tens of thousands of annotated gene sets, in human and mouse collections, for use with Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA). In toxicogenomics it is used to interpret gene expression changes through gene sets and pathways.

name: Nanomaterial physicochemical data integrated with AOP knowledge in RDF
label: nano-AOP RDF
aliases: nano-AOP RDF; vanrijn2024; From papers to RDF-based integration of physicochemical data and adverse outcome pathways for nanomaterials
creator: Maastricht University
description: An RDF knowledge graph that combines curated physicochemical data of nanomaterials from literature, with AOP information from the AOP-Wiki, using ontology terms and European Registry of Materials identifiers. A public SPARQL endpoint supports federated queries that relate nanomaterial properties to molecular initiating events and key events.

name: Nanodash
label: Nanodash
creator: Knowledge Pixels
description: Web client, previously called Nanobench, to browse and publish nanopublications: users sign in with ORCID and publish small statements from templates that are themselves nanopublications. Its FAIR Implementation Space lists FAIR Implementation Communities and their FIPs, including the PARC Toxicology FIP and the Reference AOP FIP.

name: NanoPharos Database
label: NanoPharos Database
description: The NanoPharos database has curated dataset in a ready to modelling format of NPs,  including physicochemical, structural, assay-related descriptors and atomistic computational descriptors.

name: Nanopublication
label: Nanopublication
creator: Concept Web Alliance / NBIC
description: A nanopublication is the smallest publishable unit of information: a single assertion in RDF, packaged with named graphs that hold its provenance and publication metadata. Nanopublications get resolvable, verifiable identifiers and are spread over a decentralised server network, so machines can find, cite and reuse individual statements such as AOP or FIP declarations.

name: NORMAN Bioassays Monitoring Database
label: NORMAN Bioassays Monitoring Database
creator: NORMAN Association
description: Database of the NORMAN network for results of bioassays (effect-based methods) applied to environmental samples. It holds in vitro and in vivo effect data for river water, such as receptor activity (estrogen, androgen, glucocorticoid, thyroid), mutagenicity, cytotoxicity, algal growth inhibition and zebrafish embryo toxicity, searchable by country, site, bioassay, endpoint and effect concentration. Data providers submit results with NORMAN Data Collection Templates.

name: NORMAN Ecotoxicology Database
label: NORMAN ECOTOX
creator: NORMAN Association
description: Database of the NORMAN network with experimental ecotoxicity endpoints and quality targets from different regulatory frameworks for the substances of the NORMAN Substance Database. Experts check the reliability of studies with the CRED criteria, derive quality targets online following EC guidelines and agree on a Lowest PNEC per substance, experimental or QSAR-predicted, for prioritisation.

name: NORMAN Substance Database
label: NORMAN Substance Database
creator: NORMAN Association
description: Merged and curated database of more than 100,000 substances of environmental concern, compiled from the substances contributed to the NORMAN Suspect List Exchange. It adds harmonised identifiers (CAS, SMILES, InChIKey, PubChem CID, DTXSID), MS-ready structures and predicted properties and ecotoxicity thresholds. It supports suspect and non-target screening, prioritisation and exposure assessment of emerging contaminants in the environment.

name: NanoSafety Data Interface
label: NanoSafety Data Interface
creator: IdeaConsult LTD.
description: A FAIR-aligned interface to nanosafety data, with aggregated search and access across physicochemical, bio-nano interaction, human toxicity, omics, ecotoxicological and exposure data (Jeliazkova et al. 2021).

name: Open Authorization
label: Open Authorization
creator: OAuth community; IETF
description: An open authorization protocol with which a user lets an application reach protected resources on a server without sharing a password, through tokens of limited scope. It supports controlled access to data where authentication and authorization are required.

name: Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI)
label: OBI
creator: OBI Consortium
description: The Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI) is an OBO Foundry ontology of terms for describing biomedical investigations: study designs, protocols, instruments, materials, assays and data transformations. It supports consistent, machine-readable annotation of experimental metadata.

name: OBO Foundry ontologies
label: OBO Foundry ontologies
creator: OBO Foundry
description: OBO Foundry ontologies are a collection of interoperable, community-developed ontologies for the biological and biomedical sciences, coordinated through the Open Biological and Biomedical Ontology (OBO) Foundry. The ontologies in the Foundry are developed under shared principles such as open licences, common formats, unique identifiers, etc. The registry provides ontology metadata, persistent URLs and quality checks, so data can be annotated with reusable terms that work together across ontologies.

name: OECD Existing Chemicals Database
label: OECD Existing Chemicals Database
creator: Organisation de Coopération et de Développement Economiques
description: OECD database that tracks the chemicals in the OECD Cooperative Chemicals Assessment Programme (formerly the High Production Volume Chemicals Programme). It shows each chemical's assessment status, sponsoring countries, SIDS contacts and categories, and gives access to the published assessment profiles, reports and dossiers.

name: OECD QSAR Toolbox
label: OECD QSAR Toolbox
creator: Organisation de Coopération et de Développement Economiques; European Chemicals Agency; Laboratory of Mathematical Chemistry
description: Free software application of the OECD, co-owned with ECHA, that supports chemical hazard assessment while reducing animal testing. It retrieves experimental data from many databases, profiles chemicals and simulates their metabolism, and groups them into categories of analogues, so that data gaps can be filled by read-across, trend analysis or QSAR models and the results reported transparently, for example for regulatory use.

name: OECD Test Guidelines
label: OECD Test Guidelines
creator: OECD
description: The OECD Guidelines for the Testing of Chemicals, internationally agreed test methods for the physical-chemical properties, environmental fate, ecotoxicity and health effects of chemicals, used in regulatory safety testing and accepted between countries under the OECD Mutual Acceptance of Data.

name: OECD Harmonised Templates (OHTs)
label: OECD harmonized template
creator: Organisation de Coopération et de Développement Economiques
description: Standard data formats, published with XML schemas, for reporting summaries of studies on the physicochemical properties, environmental fate and (eco)toxicological effects of chemicals. Implemented in systems such as IUCLID, they let governments and industry exchange test summary data electronically in one harmonised structure.

name: OMERO
label: OMERO
creator: University of Dundee & Open Microscopy Environment
description: OMERO is an enterprise image data management platform that enables access, processing, sharing, analysis and where appropriate publication of scientific image data and metadata.

name: OMEX (COMBINE archive format)
label: OMEX
creator: COMBINE
description: OMEX (the COMBINE archive format) is a ZIP-based container with a manifest that packs all files of a modelling project (models, simulation descriptions, data and metadata) into one exchangeable file. It lets computational models and their simulation experiments be shared and reproduced as a single package.

name: OECD Omics Reporting Framework (OORF)
label: OORF
creatorType: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: OECD
description: An OECD reporting framework that sets out what to report for transcriptomics and metabolomics data from laboratory toxicology studies, from study design and data acquisition to processing and statistical analysis. It makes omics data transparent and reproducible enough for regulators to evaluate and use.

name: OpenAIRE
label: OpenAIRE
description: OpenAIRE, a European open science infrastructure whose services aggregate and link publications, datasets, software, projects and funders in the OpenAIRE Graph and support open access and open science monitoring.

name: EFSA OpenFoodTox
label: EFSA OpenFoodTox
creator: EFSA
description: EFSA's open chemical hazards database. For each substance it summarises the identity, the EFSA outputs and legal background, and the critical endpoints, reference points and health-based guidance values from EFSA risk assessments. It is released as downloadable open data and dashboards (built on IUCLID since OpenFoodTox 3.0 in 2026), so the hazard data can be reused, for example in QSAR and read-across work.

name: OpenRiskNet e-infrastructure
label: OpenRiskNet e-infrastructure
creator: OpenRiskNet consortium
description: The OpenRiskNet e-infrastructure offered virtual research environments where containerised data and modelling services for predictive toxicology and risk assessment could be discovered, combined and deployed. The services had documented APIs and semantic annotation, and environments could run on workstations or on public and in-house clouds.

name: OpenTox data model (API)
label: OpenTox data model (API)
creator: OpenTox consortium (Douglas Connect)
description: The web-service API and data model of the OpenTox framework, defining REST interfaces and RDF/OWL representations for compounds, datasets, features, algorithms, models and validation in predictive toxicology. It enabled interoperable, distributed toxicity prediction services and was later reused and extended for nanomaterials by eNanoMapper.

name: Open Researcher and Contributor ID
label: ORCID
creator: ORCID
description: ORCID is a non-profit registry that gives researchers a free, persistent identifier, the ORCID iD, and a record linking that iD to their research activities and outputs. Its public and member APIs let publishers, funders and repositories put unambiguous person identifiers into metadata.

name: The Open Science Framework
label: The Open Science Framework
creator: Center for Open Science
description: The Open Science Framework (OSF) is a free, open-source research management and collaboration platform developed by the Center for Open Science (COS). It is designed to support transparent, reproducible, and shareable research throughout the entire research lifecycle

name: OWL (Web Ontology Language)
label: OWL (Web Ontology Language)
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: W3C
description: The W3C Web Ontology Language, used to write ontologies with formal, logic-based meaning that software can reason over; it is layered on RDF. Most biomedical ontologies, including the eNanoMapper ontology and other ontologies used in toxicology, are built and shared in OWL, which makes annotations semantically interoperable.

name: European Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals (PARC)
label: PARC
span: Data generation; Data integration; Regulatory assessment
subdomains: AOP-based mechanistic knowledge; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: EU Horizon Europe partnership
description: EU public-public partnership that develops and brings novel assessment methods and next-generation risk assessment tools into regulatory practice.

name: PARC Toxicology FAIR Implementation Profile
label: PARC Toxicology FIP
aliases: PARC Toxicology FIP; Toxicology specific FIPs (PARC)
creatorType: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: PARC (Chemicals Toxicology Community)
description: This is the FAIR Implementation Profile of the PARC Chemicals Toxicology Community. It declares which FAIR-enabling resources the community uses for each FAIR principle and is published as machine-readable nanopublications from the FIP Wizard.

name: PARC Human Biomonitoring FAIR Implementation Profile
label: PARC Human Biomonitoring FAIR…
creatorType: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
creator: PARC (Human Biomonitoring community)
description: The FAIR Implementation Profile of the PARC Human Biomonitoring community. It declares which FAIR-enabling resources the community uses for human biomonitoring data for each FAIR principle and is published as machine-readable nanopublications from the FIP Wizard.

name: PARC exchange standard for FAIR PBK models
label: PARC exchange standard for FAIR PBK…
aliases: An exchange standard for FAIR PBK models in chemical risk assessment
creator: PARC (European Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals)
description: A community exchange standard, developed within PARC, for encoding and annotating physiologically based kinetic (PBK) models used in chemical risk assessment, building on the SBML model format. It lets PBK models be shared, understood and reused across software tools in line with the FAIR principles.

name: INERIS - Chemical Substances Portal
label: INERIS - Chemical Substances Portal
creator: INERIS (French National Institute for Industrial Environment and Risks)
description: French INERIS portal that brings together toxicological, ecotoxicological, physico-chemical, environmental fate and behaviour, production and use data, and regulatory information on chemical substances produced by national and international reference organisations. It includes INERIS toxicological and environmental data sheets, acute toxicity thresholds for accidents and environmental quality standards, mainly in French.

name: PRoteomics IDEntifications database
label: PRIDE
description: The PRoteomics IDEntifications (PRIDE) database (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/) at the European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI, Hinxton, Cambridge, UK) is a centralised, standards-compliant, public data repository for mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics data.

name: Protein Ontology (PRO)
label: Protein Ontology (PRO)
creator: PRO Consortium (Protein Information Resource: Georgetown University / University of Delaware)
description: The Protein Ontology (PRO) is an ontology of protein entities, from families to gene-specific forms, isoforms, post-translationally modified forms and complexes, each with a stable identifier. It allows precise annotation of the exact protein form involved, for instance in pathway or key-event descriptions.

name: PubChem
label: PubChem
subdomains: conventional toxicology; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: NCBI, US National Library of Medicine (NIH)
description: Open chemistry database of the US National Library of Medicine. Its linked Substance, Compound and BioAssay records, contributed by hundreds of depositors, cover structures, identifiers, properties, bioactivity screening results (including Tox21), safety and toxicity information, patents and literature, with web and programmatic access. It is a central hub for chemical identifiers and data in toxicology.

name: PubChem Compound Identification
label: PubChem CID
description: The PubChem Compound Identifier (CID) is the integer accession that NCBI's PubChem gives to each unique chemical structure, obtained by standardising the structures in depositors' substance records. Registered at identifiers.org under the prefix pubchem.compound, a CID can be cited as a compact identifier that resolves to the compound's PubChem record, so data and metadata can refer to a chemical unambiguously.

name: Wikidata Identifier
label: Wikidata Identifier
creator: Wikimedia Deutschland; Wikimedia Foundation
description: A QID is the persistent identifier of a Wikidata item: the letter Q followed by a number, resolvable as a wikidata.org URI. It names a concept, entity or object unambiguously, so metadata can point to it and link to the item's statements and external identifiers.

name: QSAR DataBase
label: QSAR DataBase
creator: University of Tartu (Institute of Chemistry)
description: Open repository of (Q)SAR and QSPR models and their data, stored in the open QsarDB format with persistent handles. Published models can be archived, cited, inspected, visualised and re-run for new predictions, which makes in silico models reusable.

name: RDF (Resource Description Framework)
label: RDF (Resource Description Framework)
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; PARC Toxicology FIP
creator: W3C
description: The W3C Resource Description Framework is a graph data model that states facts as subject-predicate-object triples named by IRIs. It underlies linked data, so toxicology resources such as AOP-Wiki RDF and AOP-DB can be merged with other data and queried across sources.

name: RDMkit
label: RDMkit
creator: ELIXIR
description: ELIXIR's open, community-written toolkit of research data management guidance for the life sciences, organised by data life-cycle stage, role and scientific domain, with links to relevant tools and standards. It helps researchers and data stewards choose the practices, metadata standards and repositories that make data FAIR.

name: RDMkit toxicology page
label: RDMkit toxicology page
creator: ELIXIR Toxicology Community
description: This is the toxicology domain page of the ELIXIR RDMkit. It explains data management problems and solutions for in vitro, animal, human and ecotoxicology data, and points to relevant standards, databases and tools; its resource list is mirrored as a FAIRsharing collection.

name: ReadEDTest
label: ReadEDTest
creator: Université Paris Cité (OBERON); Pepper
description: An online self-assessment questionnaire, made in the H2020 OBERON project, for developers of in vitro and zebrafish embryo test methods for endocrine disruptors. Its seven sections ask for the information that validating bodies request, such as the test method description, data management, reproducibility, historical data and SOPs, and its scores show whether the method is ready for validation.

name: FAIR Cookbook recipe: Annotating AOP Key Events with ontology terms
label: FAIR Cookbook recipe: Annotating AOP…
creator: ELIXIR Toxicology Community (INTOXICOM)
description: A FAIR Cookbook recipe, proposed on GitHub and not yet published, on annotating AOP-Wiki key events with ontology terms for process, object, action, cell type and organ, so that key event annotations are consistent and AOPs more interoperable.

name: Metadata for cell-based assays using Bioassay Ontology (BAO)
label: Metadata for cell-based assays using…
creator: ELIXIR Toxicology Community (INTOXICOM)
description: A FAIR Cookbook recipe, proposed on GitHub and not yet published, setting out minimum and desirable metadata for cell-based toxicology assays and how to annotate them with BioAssay Ontology terms, so that the data can be found and linked to AOPs.

name: R-ODAF (Omics Data Analysis Framework for Regulatory application)
label: R-ODAF
aliases: R-ODAF; omics data analysis framework for regulatory application
creator: Maastricht University; Health Canada (Cefic LRI C4 project)
description: R-ODAF is an open-source pipeline with extra filtering criteria that turns raw transcriptomics data (RNA-seq, TempO-Seq, microarray) into reproducible lists of differentially expressed genes. It was designed so that omics data can be accepted in regulatory hazard assessment.

name: Research Organization Registry
label: ROR
creator: California Digital Library; Crossref; DataCite
description: The Research Organization Registry is an open, community-led registry that assigns persistent identifiers (ROR IDs) to research organisations. It publishes their names, locations and relationships as CC0 data through an open API, so affiliations and funders in metadata become unambiguous and machine-readable.

name: Research Resource Identifier (RRID)
label: Research Resource Identifier (RRID)
creator: University of California San Diego (SciCrunch); Resource Identification Initiative (FORCE11)
description: Research Resource Identifiers (RRIDs) are persistent identifiers for key research resources such as antibodies, cell lines, model organisms, plasmids, tools and core facilities. Authors cite them in methods sections; a central portal and resolver make each resource findable and its use in the literature traceable.

name: S2CIE (semantic, syntactic, and context-based information extraction)
label: S2CIE
creator: Universitat Rovira i Virgili (IISPV)
description: S2CIE is a web platform and API that annotates PubMed abstracts word by word with grammar, entity types and dependencies. It supports rule-based and semantic searches to extract mechanistic evidence, such as stressor-event links and key event relationships, for AOP development.

name: Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML)
label: SBML
subdomains: AOP-based mechanistic knowledge; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: SBML community (COMBINE); originated at Caltech (ERATO Kitano project)
description: The Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML) is an XML exchange format for computational models of biological processes, such as biochemical reaction networks. It lets models be shared, reused and simulated across many software tools.

name: schema.org
label: schema.org
description: Schema.org is a shared vocabulary of types and properties for describing people, places, events, datasets and other things as structured data in web pages, written in JSON-LD, RDFa or Microdata. Google, Microsoft and Yahoo! started it in 2011 and Yandex joined later that year; it is now developed openly through a W3C community group. Search engines and other applications read this markup, and Bioschemas builds its life-science profiles on it.

name: SciRAP (Science in Risk Assessment and Policy)
label: SciRAP
creator: Karolinska Institutet; Stockholm University
description: A web resource from Karolinska Institutet and Stockholm University. It offers criteria and tools for evaluating the reliability and relevance of in vivo, in vitro, ecotoxicity (CRED) and epidemiological studies, plus reporting checklists for researchers. It makes study evaluations transparent and helps academic studies report what regulatory risk assessment needs.

name: SED-ML (Simulation Experiment Description Markup Language)
label: SED-ML
creator: SED-ML community (COMBINE); initiated at EMBL-EBI
description: SED-ML is an XML format for describing simulation experiments on computational models: which models to use, how to change them, which simulations to run and which outputs to produce. It makes model-based simulation results reproducible across software tools.

name: SimpleTox
label: SimpleTox
creator: US FDA NCTR
description: Spreadsheet-based format of FDA NCTR for the summary-level animal toxicology study data that accompany toxicogenomics experiments, with the main fields of CDISC SEND combined and extracted. It was the data import format of ArrayTrack and was used for study data from the MAQC project onwards; the diXa project later adapted its fields in ISA-Tab.

name: Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry Specification Format
label: SMILES
creator: David Weininger (US EPA Duluth) and Daylight Chemical Information Systems; OpenSMILES by the Blue Obelisk community
description: Line notation that writes a chemical structure as a short ASCII string, with canonical and isomeric forms and an open community specification (OpenSMILES). It is used to exchange, store and search structures and as input to QSAR, read-across and other in silico toxicology tools.

name: SPARQL 1.1 Protocol
label: SPARQL 1.1 Protocol
creator: W3C
description: The W3C query language and protocol for RDF data. Through SPARQL endpoints, people and software can query and combine linked datasets, such as AOP-Wiki RDF and AOP-DB RDF, in a standard way.

name: SPDX License List
label: SPDX License List
creator: Linux Foundation
description: SPDX License List is a standardised, machine‑readable, controlled vocabulary of licence identifiers used across software, data, hardware, and documentation ecosystems.

name: Substances in Preparations In the Nordic countries SPIN
label: SPIN
creator: Nordic Council of Ministers (Chemicals Group) with the product registers of Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland
description: Public database on the use of chemical substances in products in Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland. It is derived from the national product registers without disclosing confidential information and gives tonnages, numbers of products, industry sectors (NACE) and use categories per substance and year, online and as a downloadable offline database. It supports exposure assessment and regulatory prioritisation of chemicals.

name: Toxin and Toxin Target Database
label: T3DB
creator: University of Alberta
description: Bioinformatics knowledgebase of common toxic substances, such as pollutants, pesticides, drugs and food toxins. Each toxin record links to its protein targets, mechanisms of action, toxicity values, and chemical and spectral data, and can be searched by text, structure or sequence. It was later presented as the Toxic Exposome Database. Potential applications of T3DB include toxin metabolism prediction, toxin/drug interaction prediction, and general toxin hazard awareness by the public, making it applicable to various fields. Overall, the variety and accessibility of the T3DB make it a valuable resource for both the casual user and the advanced researcher.

name: Tox Biology Checklist
label: Tox Biology Checklist
creatorType: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
creator: NIEHS-led working group (with US EPA and US FDA NCTR)
description: A checklist of the information that should accompany data from a toxicology or toxicogenomics study: subject characteristics, treatment and sample collection, husbandry and disposition, and the study timeline. It was proposed so that study data deposited in databases such as CEBS ( Chemical Effects in Biological Systems) could be interpreted and compared across studies.

name: TeMOwl
label: TeMOwl
creator: Fraunhofer Institute for Algorithms and Scientific Computing
description: TeMOwl is a Fraunhofer SCAI API service that gives one programmatic access point to controlled vocabularies, terminologies and ontologies from different providers, and maps equivalent concepts across them. In OpenRiskNet it was used to map identifiers and names to concepts.

name: ELIXIR TeSS
label: ELIXIR TeSS
description: TeSS (Training eSupport System) is ELIXIR's online registry of life-science training. It collects descriptions of training events and materials from ELIXIR Nodes and other providers, automatically (for example by harvesting Bioschemas markup) or by manual registration, and makes them searchable through a portal, an API and embeddable widgets.

name: OECD Test Guideline 236 (Fish Embryo Acute Toxicity test)
label: OECD TG 236
creator: OECD
description: OECD Test Guideline 236, the Fish Embryo Acute Toxicity (FET) test, which determines the acute toxicity of chemicals to the embryonic stages of zebrafish (Danio rerio).

name: Open Toxicogenomics Project-Genomics Assisted Toxicity Evaluation system
label: Open TG-GATEs
creatorType: Wet-lab research; In silico research; Regulator
creator: Japanese Toxicogenomics Project (NIBIO/NIBIOHN, NIHS and 15 pharmaceutical companies)
description: Toxicogenomics database from the Japanese Toxicogenomics Project with microarray gene expression, blood chemistry, haematology and pathology data for 170 compounds, tested in rats and in rat and human primary hepatocytes. It could be searched by compound or pathological finding, with raw CEL files for download. The original site has closed; the data remain in the Japanese Life Science Database Archive.

name: Tox Template User Guide
label: Tox Template User Guide
creator: PARC Toxicology Community
description: The user guide is meant for researchers in various PARC projects (funded under the Horizon Europe: Grant agreement N. 101057014) working on generating data from conventional in vitro toxicity assessments to fill data reporting templates so that data reported  is FAIR.

name: ToxBank Data Warehouse
label: ToxBank Data Warehouse
creator: SEURAT-1 ToxBank consortium
description: Data warehouse of the SEURAT-1 research cluster for the in vitro and omics data and protocols of its seven FP7 projects on repeated dose systemic toxicity, built on ISA-Tab, RESTful web services, RDF and the OpenTox standards. The toxbank.net site survives only as an archive.

name: ELIXIR Toxicology FAIRsharing collection
label: ELIXIR Toxicology collection
span: Data generation; Data integration; Regulatory assessment
creator: ELIXIR Toxicology Community
description: This FAIRsharing collection, curated by the ELIXIR Toxicology Community, groups standards, databases and policies relevant to toxicology and chemical risk assessment, making them easier to find, compare and reuse.

name: ToxMCP
label: ToxMCP
creator: Institute for Risk Assessment Sciences, Utrecht University
description: Suite of open-source Model Context Protocol servers through which AI assistants and other clients query toxicology data and run tools such as EPA CompTox, AOP-Wiki, the OECD QSAR Toolbox, ADMETlab and PBPK models over one structured interface, with results linked to their sources.

name: Toxicology Data Markup Language
label: ToxML
creator: Leadscope; Lhasa Limited
description: An open XML schema with a controlled vocabulary for recording toxicity studies and endpoints (e.g. genetic toxicity, carcinogenicity, repeated-dose toxicity) in enough detail for database integration and (Q)SAR modelling. Leadscope developed it and Lhasa Limited later hosted it; it gave toxicity data from different sources a common exchange structure. Its website is no longer online.

name: ToxRTool (Toxicological data Reliability assessment Tool)
label: ToxRTool
creator: EC JRC (ECVAM); FoBiG
description: An Excel-based tool, made in an ECVAM-funded project, with criteria for judging the reliability of in vivo and in vitro toxicity studies and assigning them to Klimisch categories 1 to 3. It makes reliability judgements explicit and harmonised, which supports reuse of published and non-guideline studies in regulatory assessment.

name: ToxTemp
label: ToxTemp
creator: University of Konstanz (EU-ToxRisk)
description: A structured template, developed within EU-ToxRisk and aligned with OECD GD 211, for describing cell-based toxicological test methods comprehensively and in a standard order. It suggests the metadata needed to judge the readiness, relevance and reliability of in vitro methods and their data for regulatory use.

name: ToxTempAssistant
label: ToxTempAssistant
description: ToxTempAssistant is an LLM-based tool that is designed to generate draft documents to record systematically experimental data generation and analysis. The aim is to allow toxicologists to focus on reviewing and refining content rather than performing repetitive manual data entry. ToxTempAssistant functions exclusively as a documentation aid and does not make medical or legal decisions.

name: TXG-MAPr
label: TXG-MAPr
subdomains: conventional toxicology; toxicogenomics; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: vdWater-Callegaro lab, LACDR, Leiden University
description: TXG‑MAPr is an interactive R Shiny–based bioinformatics platform designed to make toxicogenomic data interpretation intuitive, mechanistic, and test‑system specific. Built on large transcriptomic datasets, TXG‑MAPr organizes high‑dimensional gene expression data into biologically meaningful gene co‑expression network modules using Weighted Gene Co‑expression Network Analysis (WGCNA).

name: Uber Cross-Species Anatomy Ontology
label: UBERON
creator: UBERON Team
description: An integrated cross-species anatomy ontology representing a variety of entities classified according to traditional anatomical criteria such as structure, function, and developmental lineage. The ontology includes comprehensive relationships to taxon-specific anatomical ontologies, allowing integration of functional, phenotype and expression data.

name: UniProt
label: UniProt
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; FAIRsharing Toxicology collection
creator: UniProt Consortium (EMBL-EBI, SIB, PIR)
description: A comprehensive, freely available resource of protein sequences and functional information. It combines the expert-curated Swiss-Prot and the automatically annotated TrEMBL (unreviewed) sections with the UniRef clusters and the UniParc archive. Its stable accessions and many cross-references are used to identify proteins unambiguously when annotating models, pathways and mechanistic toxicology data.

name: VHP4Safety Platform
label: VHP4Safety Platform
aliases: Virtual Human Platform for safety assessment; VHP
subdomains: conventional toxicology; toxicogenomics; AOP-based mechanistic knowledge; computational and predictive toxicology
creator: VHP4Safety consortium
description: Central web application of the VHP4Safety project for human-based chemical safety assessment. It gives access to the tools, methods and data used in the project, such as AOP, QSPR, PBK and toxicogenomics tools, and shows them at work in three case studies: kidney, Parkinson's disease and thyroid.

name: Wikidata
label: Wikidata
creator: Wikimedia Deutschland; Wikimedia Foundation
description: Wikidata is a free, collaboratively edited knowledge base that stores structured statements about items under persistent Q identifiers and publishes them under CC0. It links each item to identifiers in external databases and to Wikimedia projects, so entities can be found, cross-referenced and queried by people and software.

name: WikiPathways
label: WikiPathways
sources: ELIXIR Toxicology Community; FAIRsharing Toxicology collection
creator: Maastricht University; Gladstone Institutes
description: An open, community-curated database of biological pathways, edited collaboratively and released under CC0 in machine-readable formats such as GPML and RDF. Pathway elements are linked to gene, protein and metabolite identifiers, so the pathways support omics enrichment analysis and links to adverse outcome pathways.

name: WikiPathways AOP Portal
label: WikiPathways AOP Portal
creator: WikiPathways (BiGCaT/TGX, Maastricht University)
description: The AOP community portal of WikiPathways, which collects the molecular pathway models that underlie AOP-Wiki Key Events, including molecular AOPs. It links Key Events to curated, identifier-mapped pathways, so that omics data can be analysed and visualised in the context of an AOP.

name: WorkflowHub
label: WorkflowHub
creator: ELIXIR; University of Manchester
description: WorkflowHub is a registry for describing, sharing and publishing computational workflows, independent of the workflow management system used. It builds on open standards such as RO-Crate, CWL, Bioschemas and the GA4GH TRS API to make workflows findable and reusable.

name: WikiPathways RDF
label: WikiPathways RDF
creator: WikiPathways
description: WikiPathways RDF is the Resource Description Framework (RDF) representation of the WikiPathways database, designed to make biological pathway knowledge machine-readable, interoperable, and queryable using Semantic Web technologies

name: eXtensible Markup Language Schema
label: XMLS
creator: W3C
description: The W3C language for defining which elements, attributes and data types an XML document may contain. Schemas let software validate XML files and exchange them in an agreed structure, which supports interoperable exchange of data and metadata.

name: Zenodo
label: Zenodo
description: Zenodo is a general-purpose open repository, built and run by CERN with OpenAIRE, where researchers from any discipline deposit datasets, software, publications and other research outputs. Each upload gets a DataCite DOI so it can be cited. GitHub repositories can be archived automatically, and records can be grouped in communities and linked to funder grants.
